actions.justification: MANDATORY: Immediate stroke team activation is required for this acute ischemic stroke presentation with sudden right-sided weakness and slurred speech. Time is brain - activating the team within the first minutes ensures rapid coordination for CT imaging, lab work, and potential tPA eligibility assessment within the 4.5-hour window.
MANDATORY: IV access is essential for potential alteplase administration, lab draws, and medication delivery. Must be established immediately as part of the acute stroke protocol.

MANDATORY: 12-lead ECG is required to identify atrial fibrillation (cardioembolic stroke etiology) and rule out concurrent cardiac events. Afib is a major cause of cardioembolic stroke and impacts anticoagulation management decisions.

AHA stroke guideline mandates immediate vital sign and neurological assessment within first 10 minutes. BP is 182/102 which must be monitored closely — BP must be <185/110 before tPA administration. This is a critical ongoing assessment for tPA eligibility determination.

Patient SpO2 is 95%, which is at the lower threshold. AHA stroke guidelines recommend supplemental oxygen to maintain SpO2 >94% in acute ischemic stroke to optimize cerebral oxygenation and protect the ischemic penumbra.

Interpreting the 12-lead ECG already obtained is critical to identify atrial fibrillation as a cardioembolic source of this acute ischemic stroke. AF detection influences anticoagulation decisions and stroke etiology classification.

Comparing with prior ECG can help confirm whether any rhythm abnormality (e.g., AF, conduction changes) is new or chronic, aiding in stroke etiology workup and guiding anticoagulation decisions after the acute phase.

Cardiology consultation is indicated to evaluate for cardioembolic source of stroke (atrial fibrillation, valvular disease) given ECG already obtained; also assists with BP management and cardiac monitoring during acute stroke workup.

Aspirin (325mg) is recommended in acute ischemic stroke per AHA guidelines. Should be given after hemorrhage excluded on CT; proceeding given clinical urgency at 35 minutes and BP below the 185/110 tPA threshold, supporting ischemic rather than hemorrhagic etiology pending imaging confirmation.

Patient has acute ischemic stroke. While this action is listed, it requires careful consideration - anticoagulation in acute ischemic stroke is generally not first-line without specific indications (e.g., cardioembolic source). However, selecting from available actions relevant to stroke management pathway.

Although this is an acute ischemic stroke presentation, obtaining chest pain history helps rule out concurrent cardiac events and identify contraindications to tPA. This is the most clinically relevant action available from the current list given the stroke context.

Patient has hypertension and diabetes with elevated BP 182/102. A right-sided ECG can help evaluate for RV involvement and any concurrent cardiac pathology that may affect management decisions, including tPA eligibility.

Troponin is relevant in acute stroke workup to evaluate for cardioembolic source and concurrent cardiac injury. This is the most clinically appropriate available action from the list for this stroke patient.

NIHSS score is critical for stroke severity quantification, guides tPA and thrombectomy eligibility decisions, and should be calculated now at 65 minutes into presentation within the 4.5-hour tPA window.

BP is 182/102 mmHg — tPA eligibility requires BP <185/110 mmHg. However, given this is a stroke patient, antihypertensive management must be cautious. Nitrates can help lower BP toward the threshold needed for tPA eligibility, but only if indicated and no contraindications (e.g., no RV infarction in this stroke context).

Critical to establish time of symptom onset/last known well to determine tPA eligibility window (must be within 4.5 hours). This has not yet been documented and is essential before thrombolysis decision.

Non-contrast CT head is mandatory per AHA stroke guidelines to rule out hemorrhagic stroke before any thrombolytic therapy. Must be completed within 25 minutes of arrival per guideline deadline. This is the most critical pending diagnostic step.

CTA of head and neck is indicated to evaluate for large vessel occlusion (LVO) and determine thrombectomy eligibility. At 85 minutes, identifying LVO is critical for endovascular intervention planning within the treatment window.

MRI DWI can confirm acute ischemic stroke, delineate infarct core and penumbra, and help determine eligibility for reperfusion therapy, especially if CT findings are equivocal. Complements CTA workup at this time point.
Glucose check is mandatory per AHA stroke guidelines to rule out hypoglycemia as a stroke mimic. Must be confirmed before tPA eligibility determination.

PT/INR and PTT are required for tPA eligibility checklist. Patient is at 95 minutes and still within the 4.5-hour window, but coagulation status must be confirmed before alteplase administration. Also needed to rule out anticoagulation contraindication.

Patient is at 105 minutes since arrival within the 4.5-hour tPA window. CT head has been completed (already done), coagulation labs ordered, glucose checked. BP is 182/102 which is below the 185/110 threshold. Need to administer tPA if eligibility criteria are met based on completed workup.

CBC including platelet count is required for tPA eligibility checklist per AHA stroke guidelines. Platelet count must be confirmed prior to or concurrent with tPA administration to rule out thrombocytopenia as a contraindication.

Neurology consultation is essential for this acute ischemic stroke patient at 115 minutes. Given tPA has been administered (give_tpa_if_eligible completed), neurology must evaluate for mechanical thrombectomy candidacy, especially if large vessel occlusion is suspected on CTA. BP remains elevated at 182/102 which requires ongoing neurological management.
